skill.name: pytm
skill.description: Build Python threat models with pytm, generate STRIDE findings, document trust boundaries, and produce diagrams or reports for security reviews.
skill.summary: Create threat models as Python code with pytm and STRIDE.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and reference URLs. Two findings are confirmed because the skill recommends sudo apt-get installation for Graphviz, which is legitimate but privileged setup guidance that agents should not execute automatically.

remediation.issue: Privileged package installation appears in CI and troubleshooting examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo commands with a note that users must approve system package installation, or document non-privileged alternatives where available.

remediation.issue: Several examples rely on local scripts and generated reports that may reveal architecture details.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning to review generated diagrams and reports before sharing them outside the security review group.

content.user_title: Create Python Threat Models with pytm
content.value_statement: Manual threat modeling can be slow and hard to keep current. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pytm workflows for diagrams, STRIDE analysis, and review-ready reports.
actual_capabilities: Guide creation of pytm threat models with actors, servers, datastores, boundaries, and data flows.
Explain STRIDE categories and how to review generated threats.
Show CI workflow patterns for running threat model checks on pull requests.
Provide examples for web applications, microservices, custom threats, and trust boundary analysis.
Help structure threat reports with mitigations, residual risks, and compliance context.
limitations: Requires the pytm Python package and Graphviz for diagram generation.
Does not prove that a system is secure without expert review.
Generated threats depend on accurate architecture and security attributes.
Threat reports may expose sensitive architecture details and need access controls.

use_cases.title: Model a new application design
use_cases.description: Create a pytm model for actors, trust boundaries, components, and data flows before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Automate pull request threat checks
use_cases.description: Run threat model generation in CI and flag missing mitigations during software delivery.

use_cases.title: Prepare a security review package
use_cases.description: Generate a STRIDE-focused report with diagrams, threats, controls, and follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic threat model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small web application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytm skill to help me define a basic threat model for a web app with users, a web server, an API, and a database.

prompt_templates.title: Review trust boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytm skill to review my architecture for trust boundary crossings and list the security attributes each data flow should include.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI threat model checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Add automated checks to a development workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytm skill to design a CI workflow that runs my threat model and fails when required mitigations are missing.

prompt_templates.title: Build custom STRIDE threats
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytm skill to help me define custom threats for my cloud architecture and map each threat to a mitigation and review owner.

output_examples.input: Model an ecommerce checkout service with a public web tier and internal payment database.
output: A component list that separates internet, DMZ, and internal trust boundaries.
A set of encrypted and authenticated data flows for checkout, payment, and database access.
A STRIDE review checklist for spoofing, tampering, disclosure, and privilege risks.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a threat model report for a microservices API.
output: A report outline with architecture summary, trust boundaries, threats, mitigations, and residual risk.
Recommended pytm component properties for API gateway, functions, cache, and datastore services.
Review questions for authentication, authorization, encryption, logging, and rate limiting.

output_examples.input: Check whether my threat model is ready for CI enforcement.
output: A readiness checklist for required model files, dependencies, and mitigation checks.
Suggested pass and fail criteria for unmitigated threats.
Artifact recommendations for diagrams and report outputs.

best_practices: Keep threat models in version control and update them when architecture changes.
Label sensitive data flows and protect generated diagrams and reports.
Review generated STRIDE threats with security engineers and system owners.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated threats as complete without human review.
Do not store real credentials or secret values in threat model files.
Do not publish diagrams that reveal sensitive internal architecture.

faq.question: What is pytm?
faq.answer: pytm is a Python library for defining threat models as code and generating STRIDE-based analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill create diagrams?
faq.answer: It guides pytm and Graphviz workflows that can generate data flow diagrams from a model.

faq.question: Can it run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for running threat model scripts and mitigation checks in CI.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure analysis, but experts should validate threats, mitigations, and residual risk.

faq.question: What information should I avoid placing in a threat model?
faq.answer: Avoid real secrets, credentials, private network details, and sensitive architecture information unless access is controlled.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
